Loads a picture file that contains several frames next to each other and cuts it into the frames of one image. Frames are counted from left to right, then from top to bottom, and each is `cellwidth` by `cellheight` pixels. Choose one with the frame number of [DrawImage](DrawImage).

The example makes its own sheet first with [CreateImage](CreateImage) and [SaveImage](SaveImage), so that it needs no other file.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
; Four frames of 32x32 next to each other, saved as a 128x32 picture.
Local sheet = CreateImage(128, 32)
SetBuffer ImageBuffer(sheet)
For f = 0 To 3
	Color 60 + f * 60, 200 - f * 40, 80
	Oval f * 32 + 16 - f * 3, 16 - f * 3, f * 6 + 2, f * 6 + 2, 1
Next
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
SaveImage sheet, "sheet.bmp"
Local anim = LoadAnimImage("sheet.bmp", 32, 32, 0, 4)
Cls
For f = 0 To 3
	DrawImage anim, 40 + f * 60, 100, f
Next
Flip
WaitKey
```
@param file        The path of the picture file. BMP, PNG, JPEG, TGA, GIF, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL and DDS can be loaded, see [Image formats](Image-Formats).
@param cellwidth   Width of one frame.
@param cellheight  Height of one frame.
@param first       Number of the first frame in the sheet, usually 0.
@param count       How many frames to cut out.
@returns A handle for the image, or 0 if the file could not be loaded or the frame size does not fit.
